newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil judge delays key CVRD ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil judge delays key CVRD ruling.

text.p: A Brazilian judge has asked for more information before ruling on a government appeal over the privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a court spokesman said.

The spokesman for the Superior Court of Justice in Brasilia said Justice Democrito Ramos Reinaldo had requested 10 more days in which to consider his verdict, apparently thereby delaying the lifting of injunctions against the CVRD sell-off.
The sale of 45 percent of CVRD voting shares is on hold pending the judge's ruling.
The government's next step was not immediately clear.
Planning Minister Antonio Kandir would only comment on the judge's decision after seeing the text, a spokeswoman for the National Development Bank said.
The spokesman said the judge had given the government 10 days to provide the information he deemed necessary for his ruling, but said that timeframe could be shortened.

"The (government) could speed up the delivery of the information. The judge has given them 10 days for that," he said. Asked if this meant the privatization was off for the time being, the spokesman said, "Yes".

The judge had been considering a government petition that argued a series of injunctions against the sell-off, first planned for Tuesday, should be handled by a single court because of a "conflict of interpretation" in lower courts.
